patterns.message: This layer states facts and imports nothing above itself. Anything it needs from outside — a logger, a clock, a way to read bytes — is passed in.

ONE LAYER, FOUR DIRECTORIES — bytes on a medium with a limit. What is held in memory (piece-store/), the produced segments (segment-store/), whole downloaded files (files/), and the one owner of the room all three take (storage/). They may reach each other and nothing above. Written as an exception to `../**` rather than as a list of forbidden layers, because a layer is not a directory: the blanket form cannot say "my siblings", and a list of names misses everything it forgets — `../../utils/logger.js` went straight through one on 2026-09-14.

What encoding costs is arithmetic over readings. Which sessions belong to one file, how many encoders run, what a file costs to fetch — all of it is passed in, so this can be asked without a session manager, a torrent or a disk.
What the swarm is told is decided from what is wanted (demand/) and what is held (storage/), and from nothing else.

THE MEDIA DOMAIN. A container answers for itself and hands out tracks/; a track is one stream inside one. They know nothing of torrents, encoders, viewers or this proxy's own logger: the four functions a container is built with are its whole outside world. Written as an exception to `../**` rather than as a list of forbidden layers — a list only catches what somebody remembered to write in it, and the list that stood here let `../../utils/logger.js` straight through.

THE MEDIA LAYER answers what a FILE says about itself: its containers, its tracks, where its keyframes are, and the plan for playing it. It may reach into its own domain and nothing else. What a torrent contains, which clusters may be read, where a viewer stands, what an encoder costs — all of it is passed in, so this can be asked with plain values and no torrent, no thread and no disk. Both reaches that stood here are gone: `torrent-worker/subtitle-cues.js` is now handed to SubtitleOrchestrator at the seam, and `torrent/Contents.js` is handed to the planner.
A controller translates a request for an orchestrator. Every layer below the orchestrator is reached through it, never around it.
The torrent thread serves bytes. What is produced from them, and for whom, is decided in the main thread and never asked of this one.
